intent.raw: Copy all DomainSpec skills and agents inside the repo, research the newest definitions, make the newest definition canonical, and have every runtime surface read from that canonical source.
intent.objective: Plan a governed research and canonicalization route for DomainSpec skill and agent definitions across repository-local source, root GitHub distribution surfaces, and generated runtime adapters without crossing owner boundaries prematurely.
intent.operator_sentence: First inventory every DomainSpec skill and agent source in the repo, then compare candidates by freshness and authority, select the canonical owner, and regenerate or thin-link downstream surfaces from that owner.

route_menu.context_hint: The route separates read-only research from later copy/regeneration work because implementation/domainspec is a DomainSpec-owned scope.

items.label: Research first canonicalization
items.description: Inventory every candidate, identify the newest authoritative definition, and gate copy/regeneration behind owner approval.

items.label: Direct root copy
items.description: Copy DomainSpec skills and agents directly into root .github surfaces now; blocked until owner scope and canonical source are confirmed.

items.label: Runtime adapter refresh
items.description: Regenerate downstream GitHub/Copilot/Codex packages after canonical source selection and validation.

items.label: Lean formalization lane
items.description: Inventory domainspec-lean-formalization skill and agent-prompt surfaces separately because math/Lean guardrails and authority differ from core DomainSpec workflow skills.

technique_overlays.trigger: Multiple repo surfaces contain overlapping DomainSpec skills and agents.
technique_overlays.validation_expectation: Newest-by-mtime is only evidence; canonical status requires owner, provenance, content diff, and approval record.

subagent_strategy.trigger: The route spans skills, agents, owner boundaries, and generated runtime surfaces that can drift independently.
subagent_strategy.explanation: Role-bound sibling research reduces blind spots before selecting a canonical source or copying adapters.
context: Root .github/skills has many generated or distribution-facing packages.
Root .github/agents has DomainSpec, GSD, and MARS agent definitions.
implementation/domainspec contains DomainSpec-owned skill sources and local agent/runtime surfaces.
domainspec-lean-formalization contains math/Lean-specific .agents skills and agent prompts with claim/proof guardrails.
ops/SURFACE-OWNER-BOUNDARIES.md says parent cleanup can classify child scopes but should not mutate them without an owner-scoped task.

roles.purpose: List DomainSpec, GSD, and bridge skill candidates with path, owner, mtime, checksum, and provenance hints.
List DomainSpec and adjacent agent candidates with path, owner, mtime, duplicate pairing, and runtime expectation.
List Lean formalization skill and agent-prompt candidates, preserving proof-boundary and novelty-audit guardrails.
Compare owner policy, source provenance, and existing cleanup docs before any canonical source decision.
Design downstream read-from-canonical mechanics for root GitHub surfaces, Codex installs, and generated adapters.

subagent_strategy.permission_prompt: Run five bounded subagents to inventory DomainSpec skills, inventory agents, Lean formalization surfaces, audit authority, and plan adapters before selecting canonical sources?
receipt_requirements: Each role returns concrete path evidence.
Each role separates read-only classification from mutation recommendations.
Each role names residue and blocked owner-boundary questions.

steps.name: Recover existing surface policy and owner boundaries
stop_conditions: Block mutation if the target owner scope is not named.
Flag any existing policy conflict between root-owned distribution surfaces and DomainSpec-owned implementation surfaces.

steps.name: Inventory all candidate skill and agent surfaces
convergence_criteria: Every candidate includes concrete path evidence.
Each candidate is classified as canonical-source, generated-native-runtime-package, distribution-adapter, same-checkout-facade, submodule-owned, project-owned, or cleanup-candidate.
DomainSpec skill candidates include implementation/domainspec/copilot/skills, implementation/domainspec/.agents/skills, and root .github/skills.
DomainSpec agent candidates include root .github/agents and any implementation/domainspec agent surface found by the inventory.
Lean formalization candidates are noted but kept in their own lane instead of merged into the main DomainSpec duplicate decision.
stop_conditions: Block canonicalization if implementation/domainspec cannot be inspected.
Flag generated or copied definitions with missing provenance.

steps.name: Inventory Lean formalization skill and agent prompt surfaces
convergence_criteria: Record Lean skills separately from core DomainSpec workflow skills.
Preserve claim <= proof, novelty-audit, precedent-search, Lean build, and mathlib PR guardrails from domainspec-lean-formalization/CLAUDE.md.
Classify shared utility skills such as commit-message, scratchpad, robot-talks, and test-uncommitted-changes as shared-tool candidates rather than proof-domain canonical sources.
Do not copy Lean formalization agents into root .github/agents unless a downstream runtime need and owner approval are recorded.
stop_conditions: Block if a candidate rewrite would weaken claim/proof or precedent-search guardrails.
Ask the operator before moving or copying Lean formalization surfaces into root runtime surfaces.

steps.name: Compare newest, authoritative, and duplicate definitions
convergence_criteria: For each logical skill or agent, compare content hash, modified time, provenance header, owner policy, and root adapter need.
Newest file wins only when authority and provenance do not contradict it.
Lean formalization definitions remain canonical inside domainspec-lean-formalization unless a decision record explicitly promotes a shared utility or downstream adapter.
Exact duplicates are marked for thin-link or generated-reader conversion, not independent maintenance.
stop_conditions: Block if two candidates both claim canonical authority with incompatible content.
Ask the operator if a root-owned skill has no DomainSpec-owned source but must remain available.

steps.name: Select canonical owner and approval path
convergence_criteria: Each logical definition has one named canonical owner path or a blocked reason.
Each downstream runtime surface is assigned regenerate, thin-link, copy-on-release, or delete-candidate treatment.
Approval distinguishes research authorization from write authorization.
stop_conditions: Ask the operator before rewriting implementation/domainspec, root .github, or machine-global Codex home.
Block if the decision would make a generated runtime package the source of truth.

steps.name: Plan downstream read-from-canonical mechanics
convergence_criteria: Root .github skills and agents either include provenance to canonical source or are generated from the canonical source.
Repo-local adapters do not fork body text unless the runtime requires a native package copy.
Validation checks detect drift between canonical sources and downstream readers.
stop_conditions: Block implementation if no drift-check command exists or can be added safely.
Defer machine-global Codex refresh unless explicitly scoped.

gates.condition: The route may classify implementation/domainspec and nested project surfaces, but writes require a task scoped to that owner.
A generated adapter or copied root surface cannot become the source of truth unless the owner explicitly approves that source move.
Modified time and content freshness are compared with provenance and owner policy before source selection.
Any downstream surface that reads from canonical must have a drift check, generation receipt, or explicit copy-on-release rule.
Research artifacts can recommend canonical owners and downstream readers, but cannot grant lifecycle authority without the named approval record.

boundaries.contract: Parent route may inspect and classify DomainSpec-owned source; writes require an owner-scoped task or explicit operator approval.
Parent route may inspect and classify Lean formalization skills and agent prompts; writes, copies, or guardrail rewrites require a Lean-formalization-scoped task and approval.
Root .github skills and agents are downstream distribution/adaptation surfaces unless a decision record says otherwise.

authority.lifecycle: canonical source owner selected by decision gate
authority.evidence: inventory ledger and concrete path receipts
authority.memory: memory may record the decision after explicit request only

state_namespaces.write_policy: Write only from a root-owned task-session after canonical owner selection.
Inspect from parent route; write only with DomainSpec-owned task scope.
Inspect from parent route; write or copy only with Lean-formalization-scoped approval.
Out of scope until explicitly requested.

promotion_splits.rule: Evidence supports a decision but does not change source authority without an approval record.

promotion_guardrails: Generated runtime packages stay downstream of canonical source.
Copied definitions must carry provenance or be replaced by thin readers.
Research evidence cannot mutate source authority without the decision gate.
